title: Removability of Selection Self-Loops under Observe-or-Do Intervention Families
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound exact singleton and visible-parent frontier package subfield below the field floor (paper-score ceiling 6.8 < 7.4; salvageable=false); the validity gate confirmed remaining dependency-edge and sharpness-language findings are mechanical hygiene only.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is an exact inverse-integrability characterization for a singleton self-loop, supplemented by a common-normalizer characterization for one independent visible parent and composition only for outgoing-only isolated-root contexts.

It does not establish a general contextual deletion calculus: shared latent parents, shared selected boundaries, null-event interfaces, and other multivariable boundary types remain open, so the result is materially narrower than a complete self-loop-removal theory.
paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact singleton inverse-selection criterion, canonical reconstruction, finite/countable separation, isolated-root composition, and an exact common-normalizer frontier for one independent visible parent. The package remained subfield-level because a general contextual deletion calculus and substantive application were outside the solved scope; shared-latent, shared-selected-boundary, null-event, and multivariable cases remain open.
tldr: A singleton selection self-loop is removable under the full total Observe-or-Do family exactly when the inverse-selection integral \(Z=\int g^{-1}\,dR\) is finite; randomized assigned values identify the likelihood ray, and inverse weighting gives the unique natural law. Finite alphabets and uniform positivity guarantee removal, while a pointwise-positive countable model does not. The exact extension to one incoming visible parent is parent-indexed: removal holds if and only if \(\tau(a)=\int g^{-1}\,dr_a\) is one common finite positive constant. The uniformly-positive binary witness has \(\tau(0)=4/3\) and \(\tau(1)=1\), whereas isolated-root contexts compose under arbitrary correlated joint interventions.
gap: The closest theorem, Carey et al. Proposition 12, asserts unrestricted removal of the isolated self-loop, but its proof uses a latent-value-dependent conditional normalizer as if it were one global constant. The literature does not state the resulting reciprocal-normalizability boundary or its contextual limits.
fill: Establish the exact singleton iff theorem, canonical reconstruction, finite/countable phase boundary, a uniformly-positive binary parent obstruction, and an isolated-root composition theorem. These results would replace an unrestricted deletion claim with a usable and falsifiable boundary rather than attempt a premature complete calculus.
